targets.authors: Jost, J. T., Pelham, B. W., Sheldon, O., & Sullivan, B. N.
targets.title: Social inequality and the reduction of ideological dissonance on behalf of the system: Evidence of enhanced system justification among the disadvantaged.
targets.evidence_quote: The most basic test of the hypothesis, and one that closely replicates the research by Jost et al. (2003) and Henry and Saul (2006), tests the main effect of social status on legitimacy.
targets.outcome_quote: In sum, the status–legitimacy effect is not robust and is unlikely to be the result of dissonance.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit close replication of both cited papers; overall verdict rejects the status–legitimacy effect. A single agreeing estimate does not override the overall verdict.

reasoning: Tests previously reported status–legitimacy findings with broader representative samples across years and countries. Some years overlap the original surveys, but the central test uses a different expanded sample. Footnote reanalyses are ancillary. Title, DOI and sole author verified in PDF.
